fix_commit_message:
avformat/mov: (v4) fix get_eia608_packet

The problem is reproducible with "Test for Quicktime 608 CC file.mov"
from https://samples.ffmpeg.org/MPEG2/subcc/

ffmpeg -i "Test for Quicktime 608 CC file.mov" -map 0 -c copy -y remuxed.mov

See https://trac.ffmpeg.org/ticket/11470
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 5021764413a1 on top of intro f91906973c62 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (LogicError): The get_eia608_packet function incorrectly assumes that the EIA-608 payload consists of a single 8-byte atom header followed by raw caption byte pairs. In reality, the c608 payload can contain multiple atoms (cdat for CC field 1, cdt2 for CC field 2), each with their own 8-byte header (4 bytes size + 4 bytes type). The function skips only the first 8-byte header via avio_skip(pb, 8) and then treats all remaining bytes as caption data pairs, including the headers of subsequent atoms. This causes: (1) atom headers to be interpreted as caption data, corrupting the output; (2) the hardcoded 0xFC cc_type byte always indicates field 1, so cdt2 (field 2) caption data is misidentified; (3) the size calculation ((size - 8) / 2) * 3 does not account for multiple atom headers, leading to incorrect output buffer sizing. Additionally, there is no integer overflow check on this size calculation — a crafted file with a very large sample size could cause ((size - 8) / 2) * 3 to overflow, resulting in an undersized allocation followed by a heap buffer overflow in the write loop. Root cause: The function was written with the assumption that a c608 sample contains a single atom (one 8-byte header followed by byte pairs), but the actual format allows multiple atoms (cdat, cdt2) each with their own headers. The single avio_skip(pb, 8) only skips the first atom's header, and all subsequent atom headers are misinterpreted as caption data. The hardcoded 0xFC byte also fails to distinguish between CC field 1 and field 2.
